topics.title: U.S. widens Iran economic pressure
topics.summary: The U.S. is previewing a tougher financial campaign against Iran as the war nears six months, with oil shipping and regional diplomacy still under strain.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the studio had to negotiate during a tense group project, who would read every clause, and who would try to fix the mood with coffee?

topics.title: Markets watch bond yields climb
topics.summary: Asian shares were mixed to higher while bond yields stayed elevated, showing investors remain uneasy about U.S. debt, inflation, and global oil prices.
topics.discussionPrompt: Who in the room would pretend to understand bond yields, and who would actually explain them using pizza slices and rent money?

topics.title: UK charity shops rethink the high street
topics.summary: UK charity shops face rising costs, weaker donations, and online resale competition, while still serving as community hubs and fundraising engines.
topics.discussionPrompt: If everyone cleaned out the prop closet for charity, who would donate useful stuff, and who would emotionally defend a broken lamp?

topics.title: Panama Canal faces El Niño limits
topics.summary: The Panama Canal is preparing to reduce shipping as El Niño worsens drought pressure on the waterway, adding another wrinkle for global trade routes.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the studio’s supply closet depended on one narrow canal, who would make a backup route, and who would just ration paper clips?

topics.title: Solar loans get a fresh push
topics.summary: UK ministers are being urged to cut borrowing costs for home solar panels, with supporters saying cheaper loans could lower bills and widen clean-energy access.
topics.discussionPrompt: Who would turn the studio roof into a solar project first, and who would only join after hearing the electric bill might shrink?
